narrative: Investors should watch whether Tesla’s core auto business is stabilizing while the company continues funding ambitious projects such as Optimus and the flying Roadster, especially with gasoline cars falling below 50% of global sales. The “three suppliers get paid before Tesla does” headline highlights the importance of cash generation, working-capital management, and any pressure from supplier obligations. The call should also clarify whether Musk can turn his product and autonomy promises into credible execution, since recent coverage frames Tesla as both a premium-multiple battery/technology company and a business facing competitive and cyclical pressure. Expectations appear high and volatile: optimism around Optimus, options activity, and Musk’s execution may support the narrative, but investors could react negatively if the update emphasizes slower auto growth, margin pressure, or delayed timelines.
